issues.description: The problem statement's UML declares ExcellenceLand.excellencyLevel as type double, but the solution implementation declares excellencyLevel as int. This mismatch conflicts with the requirement that constructors must accept attributes in the same order and types as in the UML and can confuse or break student implementations/tests expecting a double.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type consistent. Either update the solution and template to declare excellencyLevel as double (change the field, constructor parameter, and getter to double) to match the UML in the problem statement, or update the problem statement/UML to use int if that was intended. Preferably change the code to use double to match the UML description.
